message.content: Who were the primary figures that challenged Copernicus's heliocentric theory in the 16th and 17th centuries? Nicolaus Copernicus faced significant opposition from religious and academic authorities during his lifetime and in the centuries that followed. What specific astronomical and theological arguments did critics use to dismantle the heliocentric framework? The Catholic Church placed *De Revolutionibus* on the Index of Forbidden Books in 1616 because the heliocentric model contradicted certain Scriptural interpretations. How did scholars like Thomas Digges extend yet simultaneously critique aspects of the Copernican system? Astronomer Giovanni Battista Riccioli criticized the imprecision of Copernicus's celestial distance calculations throughout the 1600s. Did the Church formally condemn Copernicus during his own lifetime, or was the backlash a later development? Tycho Brahe, while sympathetic to questioning Ptolemy, rejected the physical reality of Earth's motion in favor of his own geo-heliocentric compromise model. What a bold and dangerous move it was to challenge millennia of astronomical consensus! The depth of resistance to Copernicus's ideas truly reveals how entrenched geocentric thought was! How revolutionary was it to place the Sun, rather than the Earth, at the center of the cosmos! One can only marvel at the courage it took to publish *De Revolutionibus* against such formidable opposition!
